newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian rebels kill 20 on bus near capital.
newsitem.headline: Algerian rebels kill 20 on bus near capital.

text.p: Algerian Moslem rebels killed 20 passengers on an overnight bus, apparently by slitting their throats, in an attack just south of the capital Algiers early on Wednesday, according to an official statement.
The Moslem guerrillas forced the bus to stop as it travelled in the Benhamdani area in Blida province at about 3 a.m.

Algerian security forces said in a statement on the official news agency APS that the 20 people were killed "in a cowardly way", the phrase normally used for attacks in which victims have their throats cut. Seven people were wounded in the raid.
The latest attack brought to nearly 60 the number reported killed in Blida province in under a week. The provincial capital of the same name is just 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers.
Nearly 200 people, most of them civilians attacked in isolated villages, are reported to have died since early November in the war between security forces and Moslem rebels.

"One way of looking at it is that they (Moslem rebels) are confining their activities to isolated areas because the cities have been made too hot for them," one senior diplomat said at the weekend, commenting on two earlier attacks on villages.
"In Algiers, people feel safer than they have for the past two years."
But he also noted that Blida province is close to the capital and that Blida town is the headquarters of Algeria's number one military district.

Authorities said rebels had killed eight civilians in the village of Amroussa, in Blida province, on Monday night. Amroussa is not far from Benachour and Boufarik villages where 29 civilians had been killed last week.

An estimated 60,000 people have been killed since violence erupted after the authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election in which the fundamentalist Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) had taken a commanding lead.

President Liamine Zeroual, pursuing his political programme in which any negotiations with fundamentalists have apparently been ruled out, has promised fresh general elections in the first half of next year.
Last month, under a massive security deployment, Algerians voted to change their constitution to legalise political parties but outlaw those based on religion. The FIS had already been banned.
